transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. Can you tell me what’s been troubling you or what brings you here today?

I guess… mostly my sleep. It’s kind of fallen apart. I’ll be in bed for hours, laptop shut, but I’m still going over work deadlines and tuition payments and class assignments in my head. And even when I do sleep, I wake up feeling like I never really switched off.
How long have you been having trouble with your sleep like this, and has it been affecting your ability to function during the day?
It’s been… about a year and three months, I think. Since I started the evening graduate certificate program while still working full-time as an analyst. It has made the days harder, yeah.
Do you find yourself feeling anxious or worried about things even when you're not actively working or thinking about deadlines or assignments?

Yeah… it doesn’t really stay contained to work or school. My mind kind of jumps around—like, am I falling behind at work, am I wasting money on school, what will my family think if I can’t keep up. Even small things start feeling like they could mess up everything.
Do you notice any physical symptoms, like a racing heart, sweating, or stomach issues, when you’re feeling anxious or overwhelmed?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t paid close attention to that… maybe I feel tense, but I don’t know about racing heart or sweating.
Do you often feel restless or like you can’t relax, even when there’s nothing specific causing you stress at the moment?
I don’t know… maybe sometimes. I don’t really think of it that way. I guess I have a hard time just sitting still or letting things go, but I’m not sure if it’s “restless.”
Do you find it hard to control your worrying, even when you try to stop thinking about things?

Yeah… I do. I’ll try to tell myself to stop and just focus on one thing, but then it kind of turns into the next worry. I end up checking my calendar or my budget or assignments over and over, and then I’m not really getting anything done.
Have you ever experienced sudden episodes of intense fear or discomfort that peaked within minutes, like a panic attack?
I don’t think so… not like that. I get really anxious, but I’m not sure I’ve had something that suddenly peaks within minutes.
Do you find that your anxiety and worrying happen more often than not, across many different parts of your life, and that they have been present for most days over the past six months or more?

Yeah… I think so. It’s not really just one thing. My mind jumps from work, to school money, to whether my family thinks I can’t handle things. Even small stuff starts feeling like it could mess up everything. It’s been… pretty constant.
Have you noticed feeling fatigued or having low energy, even if you haven’t been doing anything physically or mentally demanding?

Yeah… I do. By the middle of the afternoon at work I feel really drained, even if I haven’t done that much. Sometimes just answering emails or getting myself to the subway feels like a lot. Weekends don’t really seem to fix it either.
Have you noticed yourself becoming more irritable or easily annoyed lately, even by things that wouldn’t have bothered you before?
I’m not sure. Maybe a little, but I haven’t really been paying attention to that. I don’t think I’m snapping at people or anything.
Do you often experience muscle tension, like tightness in your neck, shoulders, or back, especially when you’re feeling anxious or overwhelmed?
I’m not really sure. I mean… I get uncomfortable sometimes, but I haven’t specifically noticed tightness in my neck or shoulders like that.
Do you have trouble falling asleep or staying asleep, even when you’re tired?

Yeah. That’s kind of… the main reason I’m here. I’ll be exhausted, but then I get into bed and I’m just lying there for hours, thinking through work deadlines and bills and class stuff. Even when I do fall asleep, I wake up feeling like I never really shut off.
Do you find it hard to concentrate or focus on tasks, even ones that you usually find manageable?

Yeah… I think so. I’ll sit with a financial model or a class reading and just realize I’ve been staring at the same thing forever. Like I’ve reread the same paragraph five times and none of it is sticking, because my mind is already off thinking about everything that could go wrong.
Would you say that you feel anxious or worried most days, and that these feelings have been happening regularly for the past six months or longer?

Yeah… most days, I’d say. It’s been pretty regular for a while now — probably about a year and three months. It started around when I began the evening graduate certificate program while still working full-time.

inference_history.note: The patient presented with sleep disturbances, mental overactivity related to stressors, and non-restorative sleep. These symptoms are common in Insomnia Disorder, Adjustment Disorder with Anxiety, and Generalized Anxiety Disorder. Further questioning is needed to differentiate between these conditions.

The duration of sleep difficulties (about 1 year and 3 months) and the context of identifiable stressors (evening graduate program and full-time work) support the consideration of F48.0 (Adjustment Disorder with Anxiety). The persistent nature of the sleep difficulties and associated distress also support the consideration of F51.02 (Insomnia Disorder). F41.1 (Generalized Anxiety Disorder) remains a candidate due to the pervasive worry impacting sleep, though further assessment is needed to rule out or confirm excessive worry beyond the stressors related to school and work.

The patient reports persistent and excessive worry across multiple domains (work, school, family, finances) occurring more often than not for over six months, difficulty controlling the worry, and associated sleep disturbance. This supports Generalized Anxiety Disorder (F48.0). Non-restorative sleep and chronic worry also align with Persistent Insomnia (F51.02). Panic Attack Specifier (F41.1) remains as a candidate due to reported anxiety, though the patient denies discrete episodes of sudden, intense fear that peak within minutes, which may rule it out if further questioning confirms absence of panic attacks.
